title: BUG: Unable to get example code working
author: dhairyadalal

comments.author: albertvillanova
comments.body:
Thanks for reporting, @dhairyadalal, and for the detailed bug report: appreciate it! 🤗 

Good catch! I am investigating the bug...

comments.author: albertvillanova
comments.body:
I think the issue was introduced in:
- #1449 

After this PR the message is no longer a typed dict, but a dataclass. I suspect that a key design consideration in that PR might have been underestimated: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/pull/1449/files#r2157218133
> Since Message and ChatMessage were mostly interchangeable, I fuse them.
One potential difficulty to consider is that the class is not a TypedDict anymore, so cannot be considered a dict.
But this didn't really create any implementation problem so far: we just handle ChatMessage objects internally, and can handle the dict conversion in Model subclasses just before sending messages to inference.

In practice, this change appears to break code paths that expect a dictionary-like structure, as illustrated by the current error:
```
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'role'
```
This suggests that somewhere, a dict (perhaps from external input) is now incorrectly assumed to be a ChatMessage instance. I suspect that during input handling, the conversion between external dicts and internal ChatMessage objects is missing or incomplete.

We may need to revisit the assumption in #1449 that handling dict conversion solely in Model subclasses would be sufficient, especially given the expectations set in the tutorials and examples.

CC: @aymeric-roucher

comments.author: aymeric-roucher
comments.body:
I think in this example the offending dict is the message you passed:  way to fix it is to just make it a ChatMessage, like:

```python
from smolagents import LiteLLMModel, ChatMessage

messages = [
  ChatMessage(role= "user", content= [{"type": "text", "text": "Hello, how are you?"}])
]

model = LiteLLMModel(model_id="gemini/gemini-2.5-flash")
print(model(messages))
```

Alternatively, one could add a method at the entrance of both `generate` and `generate_stream` methods (maybe at the entrance of `get_clean_message_list` would work) to also accept dicts as input.

comments.author: aymeric-roucher
comments.body: Found [this PR](https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/pull/1552) that implements the "accept dict-type messages in `get_clean_message_list`" solution

comments.author: albertvillanova
comments.body: Yes, I think we should support dict messages as direct input to models. I am reviewing that PR. Thanks for pointing it out, @aymeric-roucher! 🤗
